title: RuntimeDecision
description: PROPOSED, NOT ADMITTED. Separates what the grounds establish (epistemic_status) from what the runtime did (execution_disposition) and why it did it (decision_basis). The existing schemas/draft/runtime-evaluation.schema.json collapses all three into a single `verdict` field; that collapse is the defect this schema exists to correct. See adr/ADR-013.md. schemas/draft is NOT modified by this proposal.

reason_code.description: Stable machine-readable reason. Registry in docs/contracts/WARRANT-CONTRACT-v0.1.md.

epistemic_status.description: What the admitted grounds establish about the claim. ESTABLISHED: grounds establish it. REFUTED: grounds establish its negation. UNRESOLVED: grounds do not settle it, or could not be evaluated. CONTRADICTED: grounds are mutually inconsistent. UNRESOLVED is NOT a weak form of REFUTED; conflating them is the failure this field exists to prevent (I-03).

execution_disposition.description: What the runtime did. Independent of epistemic_status: a BLOCK may accompany UNRESOLVED (fail closed) or REFUTED (grounds establish the negation), and those two are not the same event.

decision_basis.description: Why the runtime did it. SUBSTANTIVE: the grounds themselves determine the outcome. PRECAUTIONARY: the epistemic state is unresolved and the system fails closed. PROCEDURAL: an artifact, binding, or availability precondition failed, so the claim was never evaluated. A precautionary or procedural BLOCK MUST NOT be serialised, reported, or reused as an established negative fact or a grounded prohibition.

reason_codes.description: Ordered, deterministic. At least one is always present, including on ALLOW.

missing_ground_ids.description: Level 1: stable proposition or atom identifiers needed for computation, as emitted by the kernel. Present whenever the kernel reported unverified grounds, INCLUDING when the outcome is ALLOW.

missing_ground_anchors.description: Level 2: human-review references connecting each missing proposition to its source and admission context. Enrichment is the OIC adapter's job, not the kernel's; the kernel is never asked to interpret source documents. May be empty when enrichment has not run, which is not the same as there being no missing grounds.

warrant_artifact_id.description: The warrant this decision rests on, or null when no usable warrant existed. Null with execution_disposition ALLOW is a contract violation.

warrant_state.description: Why the warrant was or was not usable. MISBOUND covers epoch, formula, source-version, and admission-version mismatch: the artifact is well formed but describes a different world or a different proposition.

warranty_grade_required.description: Minimum grade the envelope requires. schemas/draft/control-envelope.schema.json has no such field today; adding one is a proposed migration, recorded in ADR-013 and not applied here.

on_unknown_applied.description: The envelope's declared on_unknown policy, when it was the reason for the outcome. `deny` here means an operational fail-closed block ONLY. It is never evidence that the proposition is false, and decision_basis must not be SUBSTANTIVE when this field is set.

replay_reference.description: How to replay this decision to its exact control, admission, sources, warrant, inputs, and versions (I-15).
